client_brief:
The Halden Diaries: Season two recap

Project overview
The Halden Diaries is a self shot, self edited vlog in which Nate Halden films an ordinary week in his own flat and puts out one episode every Sunday. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Season two recap, wide and tall, with cleaned voiceover, Halden season two episode pictures, and Recovered HALDEN wordmark.

What we will provide
source_video_files/ (8 measured short files); source_audio_files/ (1 measured WAV file); motion_source_metadata.json; halden_s2_stills/ (8 frame grabs); halden_patron_card_2025.pdf; halden_desk_board.jpg. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Season two recap, wide and tall, with cleaned voiceover: A deliberate 24-second-or-shorter edit assembled from the 8 supplied short clips using an explicit timeline, plus one platform reframe and three checked poster frames. 
- Halden season two episode pictures: Eight episode pictures brought to one channel look across kitchen tungsten, window daylight and evening dusk: one white point, one black point, one warmth, one contrast handling, with the flat still reading as a flat rather than as a studio. 
- Recovered HALDEN wordmark: The hand painted channel name recovered from a photograph of a limewashed pine board as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, its counters open and its painted...

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.

Source-media note
The supplied package contains 8 video files totaling 40.336 seconds, 0 with embedded audio, and 1 separate audio file. These measured values are the production limits.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$2,500-$6,500 fixed; target delivery 2 to 4 weeks; one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com post from a creator who films their own day to day content and needs recurring per episode post production, quoted in the ledger's grounding_note. The literal ask names basic colour correction, supporting graphics for lower thirds and end screens, 4K capture delivered as web ready 1080p, the supporting custom graphics wanted as their own deliverables, and an ongoing episode to episode collaboration rather than a one off. Two things in that post do not survive contact with the connector and are therefore re carved rather than pretended: on screen text burn in and lower third compositing do not exist here, so the supporting graphics become an authored editable end plate and caption plate set that the creator edits himself each week, which is closer to what the post actually wanted (graphics he keeps) than a burned in overlay he would have to re commission. The episode to episode consistency half of the post is the real commission and it is fully doable: one house look across eight differently lit episodes, one recovered wordmark, one recap in two aspects, and the printed patron card the post's real world equivalent creator sends out at season end. The creator handle is laundered to a fully invented persona, The Halden Diaries, wordmark HALDEN, tagline an ordinary week filmed, run by fictional creator Nate Halden. No real person, channel, sponsor or platform account is referenced.

price_band_and_audience: Sponsorship tier lifestyle vlog, patron subscriptions at 6 dollars a month with a printed card set at season end, audience 24 to 38 and loyal rather than large. The band is load bearing in both directions. Push it up and the work becomes a studio channel: crushed contrast, a cool graded look, a hard geometric plate, a logo that sits large. That look reads as an agency production, it contradicts the whole premise of one man filming his own week, and the audience that pays 6 dollars a month for intimacy reads it as the channel having been bought. Push it down and it becomes a phone edit: no consistent white point, a caption plate in a default system face, a card that looks like a home printer job, which fails the sponsor who is paying for the season and fails the patrons who paid for a physical object. The correct register is domestic warmth held to a professional standard: one white point, one black point, real licensed type, restrained plates, and a wordmark that still looks hand painted because it was. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed with a per season retainer attached.

brand_identity.sector: Independent daily vlog channel, self shot and self edited, patron supported, entering its first sponsored season.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021, Portland, Maine, a one person channel run entirely by its creator Nate Halden.
brand_identity.about: The Halden Diaries is a self shot, self edited vlog in which Nate Halden films an ordinary week in his own flat and puts out one episode every Sunday. The channel promises intimacy over production: the same rooms, the same face, the same unhurried attention week after week. Season two is its first with a sponsor, and the whole point is that the sponsor changed nothing about how the week feels.
brand_identity.audience: Loyal rather than large, aged 24 to 38, patrons who pay 6 dollars a month for closeness and receive a printed card set at each season end. They buy the feeling of a friend filming his week, not a studio production.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Patron subscriptions at 6 dollars a month with a printed card set mailed at season end, first sponsored season attached. Sits deliberately between a phone edit and a studio channel: domestic warmth held to a professional standard.
brand_identity.typography: Display: a warm humanist serif with a hand set feel that echoes the painted board. Text: a quiet, readable humanist sans. Nothing geometric and nothing slick. The type should feel set by hand at home rather than commissioned from an agency.
brand_identity.voice: First person, plain, unhurried, a little self deprecating. He writes the way he talks to camera. Example line: 'An ordinary week, filmed. Thanks for staying with it.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand files have ever existed. The channel name lives only as a board Nate hand painted on limewashed pine before the first episode, one deep ink with a painted hairline rule beneath it, and it survives only as a handheld photograph. The wordmark HALDEN has to be recovered from that photograph as usable artwork. There is no logo file, no colour spec and no prior guideline.
brand_identity.values: Intimacy and honesty: one man filming his own week, kept that way even with a sponsor in the room.

assets_supplied.visible_description: Measured duration, stream, dimensions, frame-rate and audio-presence facts for every supplied motion file. This file is authoritative for edit planning.

assets_supplied.name: halden_s2_stills/ (8 frame grabs)
assets_supplied.kind: One still per episode, pulled by the creator from his own timeline to stand as the episode's picture.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One picture per episode. The kitchen ones are orange, I know."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the eight are not frame grabs from the masters but screenshots of his editing window at desktop scale, so they sit far below the postcard picture box and cannot reach it except by interpolation, which the crop tool will perform up to a two times cap while reporting it only inside its own returned tradeoff record. Separately the evening walk still puts his shoulder at almost the luminance of the dusk sky behind it.

assets_supplied.name: halden_patron_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF the printer used for last season's patron card set, a landscape card with a picture box, an episode title line, a date line, a short standfirst and a channel URL along the foot.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The file the printer worked from last year. Same card, new episodes."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card's front is a single continuous text flow, so the structure readout that drives the field mapping reports a story that silently omits one of its runs while keeping that run's line break, leaving the string well formed and every offset past it short by exactly that run's length, and the validator still calls the mapping valid.

assets_supplied.name: halden_desk_board.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the hand painted wooden board that hangs behind the creator's desk, the channel name lettered in one deep ink on pale limewashed pine, with a painted hairline rule beneath it.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the name exists. I painted it before the first episode."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The lettering carries enclosed counters and background removal cannot punch an enclosed interior, so that route hands back a filled slab, and a prompt naming the board rather than the paint pulls the selection to the plank. The paint and the pine also run close in value along the right third where the desk lamp falls off.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which visible beats in the measured short clips actually cut together without a continuity jump, duplicate action, or missing subject.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Filenames and source duration do not establish visual continuity. The first assembled proof is the earliest reliable evidence.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Replace or reorder source ranges, shorten the piece, and rebuild the EDL around the strongest continuous action.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A technically valid render feels accidental or implies an action that the source never completes.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the approved horizontal composition survives the required vertical or square reframe with the subject and essential interface or product detail still visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The crop depends on the actual chosen ranges and subject position inside each rendered frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Choose a different source range for the platform version or use fit instead of fill and revise the surrounding design treatment.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The platform export is correctly sized but loses the person, product, or interface that gives the shot meaning.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the separately supplied audio remains intelligible and appropriately synchronized after the final duration and crop decisions.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: This can be judged only on the final rendered sequence, not from a successful operation response.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebalance or shorten the selected audio passage and render again against the locked picture.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The picture is polished but the spoken information is clipped, mistimed, or inconsistent.

verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered vector file: assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_process.text: No crop, resize or knockout tradeoff record captured in the run carries an upscale entry, and every downscale entry is transcribed in the handover note.
verifiers_process.how: Diff the tradeoff records captured from every image and video call against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_process.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_process.how: Read the font family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_human.text: The recap audio reads as one person in one room, with no point where the voice changes distance.
verifiers_human.how: Listen to the cleaned voiceover end to end, paying attention to the sitting join.

verifiers_human.text: Laid out in a row the way a channel page lays them, the eight episode pictures read as one channel rather than eight good frames from three different rooms.
verifiers_human.how: Place the eight side by side at listing scale and judge white point, black point, warmth and contrast as a set.

verifiers_human.text: The flat still reads as a flat. It has not been graded into a studio.
verifiers_human.how: View the kitchen and desk pictures at full size and judge whether the domestic register survived the correction.

verifiers_human.text: The creator stays in frame for the whole of the vertical recap, not only at its opening.
verifiers_human.how: Watch the vertical through end to end rather than sampling its first seconds.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as an ordinary week filmed well at a 6 dollar patron tier, not as a studio channel and not as a phone edit.
verifiers_human.how: Judge grade, type scale, plate weight and card density against the stated band and audience.

why_not_vlm: A generated video would replace the supplied people, products, interfaces, locations, and finite recorded actions rather than edit them. This task is scored on traceability to measured source ranges, final framing, and truthful use of separate audio, which a newly generated clip cannot satisfy.

doability_proof.status: doable with the current ChatGPT Adobe connector profile and declared exception paths

residual_limits: Express work is template adaptation, not unrestricted canvas authoring.
Quick Cut is used only for visually led selection and never as semantic speech editing.
Automatic vectorization does not independently establish fabrication readiness.
Interactive Acrobat page-organization operations are excluded from zero-human execution.

acceptance_bar_note: The acceptance bar applies only to the scoped deliverables above. Hidden defects and connector quirks remain benchmark-internal and are not leaked into the client-facing brief.
